definition: In this context, high resolution refers to neuroimaging methods that capture the brain with fine detail. Such techniques can make small structures and their features easier to study, helping clarify how they relate to cognitive function.

reasons: The first sentence is broadly supported by the packet’s mention of “high-resolution neuroimaging techniques,” but the second sentence adds unsupported generalizations about making small structures easier to study and clarifying their relation to cognitive function in general; the packet only says these techniques helped elucidate the locus coeruleus’s role in cognitive function regulation.
The packet does not support the claim that “high resolution” refers to neuroimaging methods that “capture the brain with fine detail.”
